title: A GIFT IS NOT A CLEARANCE LEVEL
introLines: Before we return to the paperwork: thank you for remembering my birthday.
That gets you cake. It does not automatically get you somebody else’s personnel file.
I can point you to the proper record, confirm a limited detail, or consider showing you a restricted administrative attachment. Tell me what you are actually asking for.
choicePrompt: How far do you ask Marge to go?

messages.choiceRequired: Choose how to request the information first.
messages.cancelled: No request confirmed. Marge has not released any new information.
messages.unavailable: The requirements changed. Please speak to Marge again.
messages.confirmed: Request recorded. New lead: ask Gordon about the operation’s authorization.
messages.reviewTitle: Your earlier request to Marge is already recorded.

choices.title: Use the proper record
choices.label: Just point me to the proper record. I won’t put your job at risk.
choices.summary: You asked for an authorized route to the alias record, not private personnel material.
lines: Good. An actual request with actual boundaries. HR may survive the afternoon.
The operation’s authorization index lists “Commissioner” as an old alias used by our supervisor. Gordon. Use that reference to ask him about the authorization.
This identifies whose approval to ask about. It does not establish who typed the disputed insurance entry, and it is not a finding about John’s fate.
You have the official reference. You do not have a copy of the restricted attachment.

document.title: Authorization index reference
document.text: The authorization index identifies Commissioner as an old alias of supervisor Gordon. This reference does not identify the author of the disputed insurance entry.

choices.title: Ask for a limited confirmation
choices.label: Confirm one detail without giving me the file. I’ll keep your name out of it.
choices.summary: You requested a limited confirmation and promised to protect Marge as the source.
lines: One detail. That is a quantity I can work with.
Yes. “Commissioner” was an old alias used by Gordon, our supervisor. That is the confirmation, not permission to browse his personnel file.
The alias and the identity of the person who typed the insurance entry are different questions. Do not turn my answer to one into an answer to both.
You said you would keep my name out of it. Ask Gordon about the authorization on the strength of your own inquiry. I am not giving you a document copy.

choices.title: Request the restricted attachment
choices.label: I need the restricted administrative attachment. I’ll protect your name.
choices.summary: You requested a restricted administrative extract and promised not to expose Marge as its source.
lines: A postcard, followed by a restricted-record request. That is an ambitious birthday tradition.
I will provide an extract of the administrative attachment, not the private personnel file. It identifies Gordon as the supervisor behind the Commissioner alias.
The extract also notes that authorization material and later search records are filed separately. It does not tell you what the search found. You still have to ask Gordon.
This is not proof of who typed the disputed insurance entry, or of what happened to John.
The extract is restricted. Showing it may reveal that somebody in HR helped you. You promised to protect my name; that promise now has paperwork attached.

document.title: Restricted administrative extract
document.text: Commissioner: alias associated with supervisor Gordon. The authorization material and subsequent search records are filed separately. No search result or authorship of the disputed insurance entry is established by this extract.
